decisions.approvalNote: User explicitly selected Option C: checked by default on computers with sufficient resources and unchecked by default on constrained systems.
decisions.context: The checkbox appears only for generation-capable preparation methods. An absent preference is resolved once from a stable capacity recommendation, not continuously changed from momentary utilization. The recommendation requires decoder and schema readiness plus adequate capacity for the selected model and a safety reserve; unknown or stale facts resolve unchecked. A user toggle becomes an explicit saved preference and always wins. Checked mode fails closed without an unconstrained fallback, while unchecked mode deliberately retains prompt-guided generation followed by strict parsing and semantic validation.

consequences: Saved settings without the new field resolve enabled.
Enabled failures remain fail-closed without silent fallback.
options.label: Always checked by default
options.summary: Initialize the checkbox as checked on every computer unless the user previously saved an explicit choice.
tradeoffs: Most users receive token-level structure enforcement immediately.
Resource-constrained computers may experience avoidable latency or readiness failures.

consequences: Saved settings without the new field resolve disabled.
Prompt-guided generation remains the default compatibility path.
options.label: Always unchecked by default
options.summary: Initialize the checkbox as unchecked unless the user previously enabled it.
tradeoffs: Capable computers do not receive the reliability improvement unless users discover it.

consequences: Existing saved settings without the field resolve adaptively; explicit saved choices never get overwritten.
Unknown, stale, unavailable, or insufficient capability facts resolve unchecked.
Checked mode still fails closed and never silently falls back to unconstrained generation.
options.label: Adaptive resource default
options.summary: Initialize checked only when the selected model and runtime have adequate stable capacity and decoder readiness; otherwise initialize unchecked.
tradeoffs: Capable computers receive the safer default while constrained or unknown environments retain compatibility.
Requires a truthful, deterministic capacity estimator and clear explanation of its recommendation.
The initial state remains stable until the user changes the model or explicitly changes the checkbox.

decisions.approvalNote: User selected B3 because a visual output builder is the most user-friendly and teachable option for less technical users.
decisions.context: The generated example payload may be customized, but the outer schema version, task type, generation status, and skip controls remain host-owned. Every task-required meaning must remain mapped to exactly one bounded field so constrained decoding, semantic validation, Parquet output, saved recipes, and later training continue to agree.

consequences: The software strips protected annotations before token enforcement while retaining deterministic role paths.
Syntax and compatibility errors are shown before generation.
options.label: Guarded schema fragment
options.summary: Let users edit a bounded JSON Schema fragment for the example payload and mark required training roles with protected annotations.
tradeoffs: Offers direct schema editing in one advanced textbox.
Requires users to understand JSON Schema and custom role annotations.
Unsupported, recursive, remote, conditional, or oversized constructs must be rejected.

consequences: Both the schema and role mapping must validate and version together.
Path changes require explicit mapping repair.
options.label: Schema plus mapping grid
options.summary: Let users edit the bounded example schema and then map its JSON paths to required training roles in a separate table.
tradeoffs: Keeps standard JSON Schema separate from application mappings.
Adds a second editor, more state, and more ways for schema and mappings to drift.

consequences: Each task starts from a safe default visual template that can be reset.
Required task purposes cannot be deleted or duplicated, but their field names and nesting can change.
The generated schema preview is included in the model prompt and used by the decoder, parser, Parquet writer, and training field mapper.
options.label: Visual output builder
options.summary: Provide plain-language controls to add, remove, rename, require, and nest fields, choose basic value types and allowed choices, and assign each required training purpose; generate a read-only JSON Schema preview behind the scenes.
tradeoffs: Most approachable option and prevents syntax errors by construction.
Supports the common shapes needed for training data without every JSON Schema feature.
Requires an accessible tree editor, bounded node operations, and deterministic schema and role-path compilation.

risks: Security impact is relevant: model output, user-authored layout schemas, native dependency inputs, token masks, memory, execution time, cache state, and runtime diagnostics cross the managed Python adapter boundary.

A missing, mismatched, unsupported, or compromised dependency could weaken enforcement or prevent worker startup; exact pins, conditional Python markers, truthful readiness, direct dependency probes, provenance review, audit evidence, and fail-closed checked behavior are required.

Schema-to-grammar compilation can consume disproportionate CPU or memory; the adapter must admit only the compiler-owned subset and enforce schema bytes, depth, nodes, properties, choices, cache entries, and retained source bytes before compilation.

A stateful processor can leak state between generations or be reused with the wrong tokenizer; each generator must own its cache, keys must bind canonical schema material, processors must reset before use, and cache eviction must be deterministic.
Max-token truncation or a processor dead end can produce a JSON-looking prefix; checked generation must require EOS completion and post-validate the exact schema without unconstrained retry.

Raw dependency, compiler, tokenizer, model, prompt, or generated-output exceptions could disclose sensitive content or local paths; public failures and evidence must use bounded stable codes and safe summaries only.
